findings.summary: test_portable_runtime.py::test_isolated_real_lifecycle_and_ownership_guards fails reproducibly (2/2 runs) on the current host: after lifecycle.trigger_task() (Start-ScheduledTask, async) the registered Windows scheduled task does not execute->write a tick receipt within the 20s polling deadline. The direct synchronous subprocess run of the identical action DOES produce a tick, and the frozen candidate bytes are unchanged, so this is Task-Scheduler execution-latency/host-state sensitivity — possibly compounded by a too-tight 20s deadline — not a candidate-byte regression.
findings.open_question_for_implementer: Is this (a) a genuine RC portability defect — the scheduler-triggered runtime does not reliably fire on a real host, which a released user could hit — or (b) test fragility needing an adaptive/longer deadline or an explicit environment gate for the real-Task-Scheduler path? Distinguishing (a) vs (b) requires implementer investigation (e.g., query the task's LastRunTime/LastTaskResult after trigger; test on a less-loaded host; instrument Start-ScheduledTask -> execution latency).
